title: Shadow-traffic recalibration and pin drift remediation playbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Establish an operational playbook that uses controlled shadow traffic and targeted production samples to detect drift between published Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) and live behavior, and to remediate pin misalignments. Deliverables: (1) a repeatable recalibration procedure and thresholds for automatic profile refresh suggestions, (2) a remediation/rollback flow for pinned versions when drift violates cost or latency SLOs, and (3) an instrumentation and dashboarding spec for ongoing monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step shadowing procedures and ownership
Automated job that samples 1% production traffic to shadow model variants and logs latency/cost deltas to the profile store
Alerting rule that triggers when rolling 3-hour median latency or cost-per-token deviates more than configured thresholds (default: latency +15%, cost +20%)
Canary rollout policy that prevents automatic pin flips without manual signoff for customer-impacting models
Dashboard card in Console showing drift score, recent shadow vs live traces, and actionable remediation links
tasks: Define sampling budget and routing policy for shadow traffic (SRE + Runtime) - owner: Priya Rao
Implement shadow capture pipeline that anonymizes and prefixes traces for profile comparison - owner: Eng infra
Extend profile store schema to record last-calibrated-timestamp and drift-history - owner: Data Eng
Create alerting playbook and mapped pages in PagerDuty for model-stewards - owner: Observability
Design UI affordances in Console for initiating a profile recalibration and for flagging pinned versions - owner: Console PM
Draft policy for when automatic profile suggestions are applied vs. require manual steward approval - owner: PM
decisions: We will use 1% shadow sampling by default, configurable per-customer to limit cost exposure.
Automatic pin rotation is disallowed for P0 customer tiers; those must be manually approved.
Drift thresholds start conservative (latency +15%, cost +20%) and will be tuned after two weeks of sampling data.
Shadow requests will not hit external tools (plugins) to avoid side effects; functional mocks will be used when needed.

risks: Sampling too large will materially increase infra cost and distort cost anchors; mitigation: strict sampling caps and billing tags.
False positives due to transient infra noise (network spikes) could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigation: use rolling windows and multiple signals.
Privacy/regulatory constraints for shadowing real customer payloads in regulated tenants; mitigation: apply per-tenant opt-out and synthetic masking rules.
rollback_plan: If an applied profile update or pin change causes customer-facing regressions (confirmed via CI smoke tests or customer reports), immediately revert to previous pinned profile, throttle new traffic to the updated variant, open incident (INC-XXXX) and run root-cause analysis. Escalation path: on-call SRE -> Runtime lead -> PM -> Customer Success for impacted accounts.
notes: Tie this playbook to the existing verified-profile ledger so changes are auditable and signed.
Consider a separate lightweight flow for low-risk models (tiny models used for embeddings) that allows automated refresh after soft approval windows.
Plan a two-week gradual tuning period where thresholds and sampling rates can be adjusted without affecting pins.
